subject.title: fix: handle Claude CLI synthetic placeholders

question: Should a recognized Claude CLI synthetic placeholder immediately terminate the OpenClaw attempt and start model fallback, or should reusable sessions continue waiting for a later real result from the same process?
rationale: The same dependency-emitted marker is observed in both terminal no-output cases and nonterminal reused-session cases, so code inspection cannot safely choose one recovery policy without owner intent and live lifecycle proof.

options.title: Gate on terminal state
options.body: Keep the marker but classify it as `empty_result` only after process/session evidence proves no later result can arrive.

options.title: Accept immediate fallback
options.body: Approve the current semantics and require live Claude CLI proof that fallback cannot race or discard a later answer in reusable sessions.

options.title: Split metadata from recovery
options.body: Land only placeholder detection and defer fallback/session behavior to a follow-up that resolves https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99131.

recommendation.title: Gate on terminal state
recommendation.body: Keep the marker but classify it as `empty_result` only after process/session evidence proves no later result can arrive.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent merged parser rewrite is the strongest current-main policy precedent for empty Claude CLI results.
